editorial.headline: KBLI 46452: Wholesale Trade in Printed and Published Goods
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to PMA, but a Bali-wide risk moratorium means foreign investors cannot register it in Bali today.
editorial.body:
Wholesale trade is the commercial route through which printed and published goods move through the market. KBLI 46452 covers wholesale trade in printing and publishing goods in various forms, with books, magazines and newspapers expressly included as examples. Its subject is therefore the wholesale activity surrounding those goods: a business dealing in published and printed material across the forms named in the record. The definition is focused, but broad enough to encompass more than one kind of print publication within the same wholesale activity.

The activity is open across the full range of business scales listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That gives the code a wide operating frame, from micro and small businesses through medium and large enterprises. For a founder, the practical starting point is to match the registered activity to the wholesale trade in the relevant printed or published goods, rather than treating the code as a general label for the wider publishing economy.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In other words, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. The reference given for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is the national ceiling for the activity and should be read as such: it establishes the foreign-ownership position at the national level, not a separate local registration outcome.

Bali is where the picture changes decisively. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class) because, at the Besar scale, every scope is recorded in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk; the record says this is blocked by the Bali moratorium of 13 May 2026. That moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA across the island on a permanent basis. The national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the national position, but it does not displace Bali’s registration block for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this activity is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration in Bali today.
